literature.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 基于假病毒的中和抗体(pVNA)检测系统表现出广泛的鲁棒性、精确性和稳定性。检测限(LOD)为2.63 IU/mL(95% CI:1.81–3.84),变异系数小于20%。线性相关分析显示这些变量之间存在很强的相关性(R2 > 0.90)。 [10.1128/jcm.00877-26]
使用 DFAT 作为参考标准,Quantiplus 检测对人类和动物大脑样本表现出 100% 的敏感性和特异性,并与生前人类样本的内部 RT-PCR (Cohen’s Kappa 1) 完全一致。 [10.1007/s13337-026-00979-5]
III级暴露占所有病例的60.5%(24,322/40,222),被动免疫率为55.5%,标准初诊护理率为45.3%(11,019/24,322)。年轻人(15-44 岁)、有抓伤的患者以及就诊延迟的患者与不完整的 PEP 给药独立相关。 [10.1186/s12889-026-29132-z]
MRI 显示丘脑和颞叶典型的双侧对称灰质高信号,强烈提示 狂犬病 脑炎。此外,MRI 还发现了右侧横窦和乙状窦广泛脑静脉窦血栓形成的非典型大血管发现,这可能导致白质不对称变化。 [10.1016/j.radcr.2026.07.088]
此外,该测定法表现出分析灵敏度和特异性,支持其用于马神经系统疾病的综合病因学 诊断。 [10.1007/s42770-026-02065-w]

Using DFAT as the reference standard, the Quantiplus assay demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for human and animal brain samples and showed perfect agreement with the in-house RT-PCR for antemortem human samples (Cohen’s Kappa 1). [10.1007/s13337-026-00979-5]

Grade III exposures accounted for 60.5% (24,322/40,222) of all cases, with a passive immunization rate of 55.5% and a standard first-visit care rate of 45.3% (11,019/24,322). [10.1186/s12889-026-29132-z]
MRI revealed classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis. [10.1016/j.radcr.2026.07.088]

Furthermore, the assay demonstrated analytical sensitivity and specificity that support its use for the comprehensive etiological diagnosis of equine neurological diseases. [10.1007/s42770-026-02065-w]

news.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 经马里兰州卫生部检测后,一只海狸被确认患有 狂犬病。蒙哥马利县卫生和动物服务官员报告了这一病例,并向公众发出提醒,避免与野生动物接触。 [news-4076f7dad99c0f72]
动物中确诊的 狂犬病 病例促使发布公共卫生建议,以防止动物接触 (N14)。 [news-15458e357d3b53f8]
狂犬病 在弗吉尼亚州罗阿诺克市的一只浣熊身上得到证实。弗吉尼亚州卫生部报告了这一病例,并被视为已确诊事件。 [news-6e458528085bf743]
自 2017 年 7 月以来,狂犬病 已在砂拉越夺走了 87 人的生命,在 94 起报告病例中,死亡率高达 93%。砂拉越兽医服务部证实,今年有 23 只狗和 3 只猫的 狂犬病 检测呈阳性。 [news-b1897d4d4c00981d]
据砂拉越卫生局(JKNS)报告,自 2017 年 7 月以来,砂拉越已记录 94 例人类 狂犬病 病例和 87 例死亡,并在“停止 狂犬病 2026:狂犬病 教育嘉年华”启动期间得到副总理拿督阿玛沉桂贤博士的证实。 [news-f4055aa512212cbf]

key_findings_en: A beaver was confirmed to have rabies after testing by the Maryland Department of Health. This case was reported by Montgomery County Health and Animal Services officials, who issued a public reminder to avoid contact with wildlife. [news-4076f7dad99c0f72]
A confirmed rabies case in an animal prompted a public health advisory to prevent animal exposures (N14). [news-15458e357d3b53f8]
Rabies was confirmed in a raccoon in Roanoke City, Virginia. The Virginia Department of Health reported this case, and it is considered a confirmed event. [news-6e458528085bf743]

Rabies has claimed 87 human lives in Sarawak since July 2017, with a fatality rate of 93% among 94 reported cases. The Sarawak Veterinary Services Department confirmed 23 dogs and three cats tested positive for rabies this year. [news-b1897d4d4c00981d]

Sarawak has recorded 94 human rabies cases and 87 deaths since July 2017, as reported by the Sarawak Health Department (JKNS) and confirmed by Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian during the launch of the Stop Rabies 2026: Rabies Education Carnival. [news-f4055aa512212cbf]

papers.title: A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody assay for measuring neutralizing antibody against rabies virus
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To establish a laboratory detection assay for a human neutralizing antibody (NAb) against rabies virus and to evaluate its efficiency in human serum samples. A pseudovirus pXN2‐RABV‐G harboring the RABV G gene was applied. The precision, robustness, linearity, stability, inclusivity, and limit of detection of the assay were evaluated. The consistency and correlation of the assay with ELISA and rapid fluorescent focus inhibition test (RFFIT) were analyzed. A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody (pVNA) detection system based on the pXN2‐RABV‐G was successfully developed and showed broad robustness (culture media: χ 2 = 4.00, P > 0.05, cell passages: χ 2 = 0.25, P > 0.05), precision (independent detection: P > 0.05), lower/upper limit of linearity (0.09 to 93.73 IU/mL, R 2 > 0.95), and stability ( P > 0.05). The limit of detection (LOD) was 2.63 IU/mL (95% CI: 1.81–3.84), expressed as the lowest human sera antibody level reliably distinguishable from background signals, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%. Compared with the commercial ELISA and the gold standard RFFIT assay, the kappa values were 0.74 and 0.82, respectively, and the results were highly consistent. Linear correlation analysis revealed a strong correlation between these variables ( R 2 > 0.90). A total of 103 recipients from 2019 to 2023 were included in the serological testing and the following analysis. NAb titers were significantly correlated with vaccine dose ( P < 0.001) and the most recent vaccination time ( P < 0.001). The geometric mean titer (GMT) of the 5-dose vaccination group was greater than that of the 1-dose, 2-dose, 3-dose, and 4-dose groups (3.15 vs 3.19 vs 6.18 vs 12.21 vs 13.40 IU/mL). The established pVNA assay for human rabies NAb detection has a detection capability similar to that of the gold standard RFFIT, but it has the advantages of reduced biosafety requirements, laboratory activity, and time, which highlight its safety, high efficiency, and feasibility for screening and monitoring rabies virus antibodies after vaccination. IMPORTANCE Rabies is a lethal disease with no effective clinical treatment. Vaccination is the only way to prevent it routinely, which makes post-vaccination antibody testing essential. The current standard test requires a highly equipped laboratory, biosafety measures, and is time-consuming. This study develops a safe, efficient test for detecting rabies neutralizing antibodies using pseudovirus technology. It is comparable to the gold standard test in accuracy but easier to implement in routine labs, which enables broader use in screening and monitoring antibodies post-vaccination. This advantage addresses a key gap in rabies prevention, reducing the uncertainty for individuals with immunodeficiency who are nonresponsive to vaccination and at risk of rabies exposure.

papers.title_zh: 基于假病毒的中和抗体测定,用于测量针对 狂犬病病毒 的中和抗体
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT To establish a laboratory detection assay for a human neutralizing antibody (NAb) against rabies virus and to evaluate its efficiency in human serum samples. A pseudovirus pXN2‐RABV‐G harboring the RABV G gene was applied. The precision, robustness, linearity, stability, inclusivity, and limit of detection of the assay were evaluated. The consistency and correlation of the assay with ELISA and rapid fluorescent focus inhibition test (RFFIT) were analyzed. A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody (pVNA) detection system based on the pXN2‐RABV‐G was successfully developed and showed broad robustness (culture media: χ 2 = 4.00, P > 0.05, cell passages: χ 2 = 0.25, P > 0.05), precision (independent detection: P > 0.05), lower/upper limit of linearity (0.09 to 93.73 IU/mL, R 2 > 0.95), and stability ( P > 0.05). The limit of detection (LOD) was 2.63 IU/mL (95% CI: 1.81–3.84), expressed as the lowest human sera antibody level reliably distinguishable from background signals, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%. Compared with the commercial ELISA and the gold standard RFFIT assay, the kappa values were 0.74 and 0.82, respectively, and the results were highly consistent. Linear correlation analysis revealed a strong correlation between these variables ( R 2 > 0.90). A total of 103 recipients from 2019 to 2023 were included in the serological testing and the following analysis. NAb titers were significantly correlated with vaccine dose ( P < 0.001) and the most recent vaccination time ( P < 0.001). The geometric mean titer (GMT) of the 5-dose vaccination group was greater than that of the 1-dose, 2-dose, 3-dose, and 4-dose groups (3.15 vs 3.19 vs 6.18 vs 12.21 vs 13.40 IU/mL). The established pVNA assay for human rabies NAb detection has a detection capability similar to that of the gold standard RFFIT, but it has the advantages of reduced biosafety requirements, laboratory activity, and time, which highlight its safety, high efficiency, and feasibility for screening and monitoring rabies virus antibodies after vaccination. IMPORTANCE Rabies is a lethal disease with no effective clinical treatment. Vaccination is the only way to prevent it routinely, which makes post-vaccination antibody testing essential. The current standard test requires a highly equipped laboratory, biosafety measures, and is time-consuming. This study develops a safe, efficient test for detecting rabies neutralizing antibodies using pseudovirus technology. It is comparable to the gold standard test in accuracy but easier to implement in routine labs, which enables broader use in screening and monitoring antibodies post-vaccination. This advantage addresses a key gap in rabies prevention, reducing the uncertainty for individuals with immunodeficiency who are nonresponsive to vaccination and at risk of rabies exposure.

papers.title: Atypical neuroimaging in rabies encephalitis: A case report of concurrent cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in a nine-year-old patient
papers.abstract: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient’s condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病 脑炎的非典型神经影像:一名 9 岁患者并发脑静脉窦血栓形成的 病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient’s condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

papers.title: Analysis of the current status of animal-related injuries in the Taihu Lake region: a quality assessment of post-exposure prophylaxis in 40,222 Cases (2023–2025) and implications for areas with no reported indigenous human rabies cases
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The Taihu Lake region, a highly urbanized area in the Yangtze River Delta, experiences a high prevalence of animal‐related injuries. Within this region, Wuxi has reported no indigenous human rabies cases for over a decade. Against China’s 2024–2025 rabies resurgence, any decline in post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) quality in zero-case areas could become a weak link that ignites epidemic resurgence. This study evaluated first-visit PEP quality in the region, explored the possible risk of what we term “prevention fatigue”—a silent decline in PEP quality in areas with no reported indigenous human rabies cases—and proposed targeted intervention strategies. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we included 40,222 first‐visit cases of animal‐related injuries at our hospital from January 2023 to December 2025. Outcomes included non-use of passive immunization in Grade III exposures, failure of standard first-visit care, and delayed presentation. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations and interaction effects. Results Grade III exposures accounted for 60.5% (24,322/40,222) of all cases. Among these, the passive immunization rate was 55.5%, and the standard first‐visit care rate was 45.3% (11,019/24,322). Young adults (15–44 years, aOR = 2.17), scratches (vs. bites, aOR = 1.20), and delayed presentation (aOR = 1.49) were independently associated with incomplete PEP delivery. Significant interactions were found for age group × injury type ( P < 0.001), animal × delayed presentation ( P < 0.001), and exposure site × delayed presentation ( P = 0.019). From 2023 to 2025, passive immunization rates among Grade III exposures increased from 52.8% to 60.1% (P for trend < 0.001), whereas standard first-visit care rates were 44.5%, 42.8%, and 48.4% across the three years (P for trend < 0.001); delayed presentation decreased from 37.9% to 31.9% (P for trend < 0.001). Conclusions Persistent gaps in PEP compliance were observed in this region with over a decade of no indigenous human rabies cases. Young adults, patients with scratch injuries and delayed consultation constituted overlapping high-risk groups. We put forward two sentinel surveillance indicators and stratified intervention strategies, stressing that Grade III scratches require the same protective management as bite wounds.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景太湖地区是长江三角洲高度城市化的地区,动物相关伤害的发生率很高。在该地区,无锡十多年来没有报告本土人类 狂犬病 病例。相对于中国2024-2025年暴露后预防的复苏,零病例地区暴露后预防(PEP)质量的任何下降都可能成为引发疫情死灰复燃的薄弱环节。这项研究评估了该地区首次就诊的 PEP 质量,探讨了我们所说的“预防疲劳”(在没有报告土著人类 狂犬病 病例的地区,PEP 质量悄然下降)的可能风险,并提出了有针对性的干预策略。方法 在这项回顾性横断面研究中,我们纳入了 2023 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间在我院首次就诊的 40,222 例动物相关损伤病例。结果包括在 III 级暴露中未使用被动免疫、标准首次就诊护理失败以及延迟就诊。多变量逻辑回归检查关联和交互作用。结果 III级暴露占所有病例的60.5%(24,322/40,222)。其中,被动免疫率为55.5%,标准初诊护理率为45.3%(11,019/24,322)。年轻人(15-44 岁,aOR = 2.17)、抓伤(相对于咬伤,aOR = 1.20)和延迟就诊(aOR = 1.49)与不完整的 PEP 输送独立相关。年龄组 × 损伤类型 ( P < 0.001)、动物 × 延迟就诊 ( P < 0.001) 和暴露部位 × 延迟就诊 ( P = 0.019) 存在显着的相互作用。从 2023 年到 2025 年,III 级暴露的被动免疫率从 52.8% 增加到 60.1%(趋势 P < 0.001),而这三年的标准首次就诊护理率分别为 44.5%、42.8% 和 48.4%(趋势 P < 0.001);延迟就诊从 37.9% 下降至 31.9%(趋势 P < 0.001)。结论 在该地区观察到 PEP 依从性持续存在差距,十多年来没有本土人类 狂犬病 病例。青壮年、抓伤患者、延迟就诊患者构成重叠的高危人群。我们提出了两个哨点监测指标和分层干预策略,强调III级抓伤需要与咬伤相同的保护管理。

papers.full_text: Abstract Rabies, a fatal zoonotic encephalitis, causes approximately 60,000 deaths annually worldwide. The current gold standard for laboratory confirmation is the direct fluorescent antibody test (DFAT) on postmortem brain samples. To overcome the limitations of DFAT, real-time PCR for rabies viral RNA detection has emerged as a reliable alternative for both antemortem and postmortem samples. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of the Quantiplus Rabies Virus Detection Kit, a commercially available real-time PCR kit for detecting rabies RNA. The study included 24 postmortem human brain samples, 14 antemortem human samples (cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, and nuchal skin), and 44 postmortem animal brain samples. DFAT and Quantiplus assays were performed on brain samples, while Real-time TaqMan RT-PCR and Quantiplus assays were used on antemortem human samples. Using DFAT as the reference standard, the Quantiplus assay demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for human and animal brain samples. It showed agreement with the in-house RT-PCR for antemortem human samples (Cohen’s Kappa 1). Notwithstanding the relatively small sample size in this study, the Quantiplus assay is a reliable alternative to in-house RT-PCR for rabies diagnosis, enhancing surveillance and control efforts toward eliminating dog-mediated rabies deaths by 2030. Data availability The datasets generated during and/or analysed during the current study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. References - WHO. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Rabies, a fatal zoonotic encephalitis, causes approximately 60,000 deaths annually worldwide. The current gold standard for laboratory confirmation is the direct fluorescent antibody test (DFAT) on postmortem brain samples. To overcome the limitations of DFAT, real-time PCR for rabies viral RNA detection has emerged as a reliable alternative for both antemortem and postmortem samples. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of the Quantiplus Rabies Virus Detection Kit, a commercially available real-time PCR kit for detecting rabies RNA. The study included 24 postmortem human brain samples, 14 antemortem human samples (cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, and nuchal skin), and 44 postmortem animal brain samples. DFAT and Quantiplus assays were performed on brain samples, while Real-time TaqMan RT-PCR and Quantiplus assays were used on antemortem human samples. Using DFAT as the reference standard, the Quantiplus assay demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for human and animal brain samples. It showed agreement with the in-house RT-PCR for antemortem human samples (Cohen’s Kappa 1). Notwithstanding the relatively small sample size in this study, the Quantiplus assay is a reliable alternative to in-house RT-PCR for rabies diagnosis, enhancing surveillance and control efforts toward eliminating dog-mediated rabies deaths by 2030. analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the Quantiplus Rabies Virus Detection Kit using 24 postmortem human brain samples, 14 antemortem human samples (cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, and nuchal skin), and 44 postmortem animal brain samples.
analysis.methods: DFAT and Quantiplus assays were performed on brain samples, while real-time TaqMan RT-PCR and Quantiplus assays were used on antemortem human samples to compare diagnostic performance.
analysis.main_results: Using DFAT as the reference standard, the Quantiplus assay demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for human and animal brain samples and showed perfect agreement with the in-house RT-PCR for antemortem human samples (Cohen’s Kappa 1).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the Quantiplus assay as a reliable alternative to in-house RT-PCR for rabies diagnosis, highlighting its potential to enhance surveillance and control efforts toward eliminating dog-mediated rabies deaths by 2030.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the diagnostic performance of the Quantiplus Rabies Virus Detection Kit, a real-time PCR assay, against the gold-standard direct fluorescent antibody test (DFAT) and in-house RT-PCR. Using 24 postmortem human brain samples, 14 antemortem human samples, and 44 postmortem animal brain samples, the Quantiplus assay achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity for brain tissues and perfect agreement with in-house RT-PCR for antemortem samples. The authors conclude that the kit is a reliable alternative for rabies diagnosis, supporting surveillance and control efforts toward the 2030 elimination goal. However, the small sample size limits generalisability, warranting further validation in larger cohorts.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 24 个死后人类大脑样本、14 个死前人类样本(脑脊液、唾液和颈部皮肤)和 44 个死后动物大脑样本评估了 Quantiplus 狂犬病病毒 检测试剂盒。

papers.title: Factors associated with rabies vaccination uptake among dog owners in Butaleja Town Council, Eastern Uganda: A cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rabies remains a major zoonotic public health threat, associated with approximately 59,000 annual deaths globally, with Africa bearing 36% of this burden. In Uganda, an estimated 36 human deaths and 1.8 million dog bite exposures occur annually, yet national dog vaccination coverage remains critically low at approximately 10%. This study investigated factors associated with rabies vaccination uptake among dog owners in Butaleja Town Council, Eastern Uganda, a high-risk setting. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 173 dog owners between May 18 and June 28, 2024, using semi-structured questionnaires. The primary outcome was vaccination uptake (≥1 dose in the past year). Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimated adjusted prevalence ratios for all socio-demographic, veterinary system, health system, dog-related, and knowledge factors. Among 173 dog owners, 57.2% vaccinated at least one dog, corresponding to 54.6% (166/304) of all dogs vaccinated. Factors associated with vaccination uptake included older age (21–40 years: aPR 1.43, 95% CI: 1.15–1.71; 41–60 years: aPR 1.53, 95% CI: 1.22–1.82; ≥61 years: aPR 1.56, 95% CI: 1.33–2.23), higher education (primary: aPR 1.20, 95% CI: 1.00–1.45; secondary: aPR 1.55, 95% CI: 1.20–2.00), higher income, access to veterinary clinics (aPR 2.50, 95% CI: 1.52–3.75), and participation in community education sessions (aPR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.34–2.15). While household-level uptake showed moderate engagement, the resulting dog population vaccination coverage of 48.4% remained substantially below the 70% World Health Organization threshold required for herd immunity. Achieving the “Zero by 30” elimination dog-bite mediated Rabies target in this setting requires targeted interventions addressing the identified associated factors including; enhanced community education, improved veterinary service accessibility, reminder systems, and strategies to convert partial household vaccination into complete coverage particularly among younger, less educated, and lower-income dog owners. Author Summary Rabies remains a neglected tropical disease that claims approximately 59,000 lives annually, predominantly in Africa and Asia. While mass dog vaccination is the most effective control strategy, many communities struggle to reach the 70% coverage needed to mitigate rabies transmission. This study investigated why dog owners in a high-risk Ugandan community do or do not vaccinate their animals. We surveyed 173 dog owners and found an important gap; while 57% of owners had vaccinated at least one dog, only 48% of all dogs were actually vaccinated far below the global target. This distinction matters because it shows that even owners who participate in vaccination programs often leave some dogs unprotected, undermining efforts to achieve herd immunity. Several factors were associated with vaccination. Owners with better access to veterinary clinics, knowledge of where to get vaccines, and participation in community education were more likely to vaccinate. Receiving vaccination reminders also made a significant difference. Conversely, limited awareness, poor service accessibility, and socioeconomic challenges prevented many from vaccinating their dogs. These findings point to practical solutions: improving communication about vaccination locations, sending reminders, and strengthening community education could help more families fully vaccinate all their dogs. For Uganda and similar settings, addressing these barriers is essential to reach the global goal of eliminating rabies deaths by 2030.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 2024年5月18日至6月28日期间,使用半结构化问卷对173名狗主人进行了横断面调查。使用具有稳健方差的修正泊松回归来估计影响 疫苗接种 吸收的因素的调整后的 患病率 比率。

papers.title: Immunogenicity in dogs vaccinated against rabies with a highly safe and efficacious 3rd generation oral rabies vaccine in longitudinal and cross-sectional studies
papers.abstract: Although oral vaccination of dogs against rabies is considered a promising and beneficial approach, the effectiveness of oral rabies vaccines inducing a protective (humoral) immune response in local free-roaming dogs is often questioned. To address concerns regarding this issue, an analysis was conducted to evaluate the immunogenicity and serological response to the oral rabies vaccine strain SPBN GASGAS in dogs. Serological data from longitudinal and cross-sectional studies conducted under both experimental and field conditions were analysed. Factors influencing the post-vaccination serological response, including bait matrix, sachet type, vaccine titre, and dog origin, were compared, and challenges and limitations in the serological assessment of oral vaccination in dog populations were examined. In addition, the kinetics of rabies virus-binding antibodies following vaccination were analysed and interpreted in the context of SPBN GASGAS-induced rabies-specific immunoglobulin classes. The analyses demonstrate that free-roaming dogs, irrespective of origin, develop a measurable, consistent, and long-lasting humoral immune response following vaccination with SPBN GASGAS. This response is comparable to that observed in dogs under experimental conditions and non-inferior to that induced by parenteral administration of inactivated rabies vaccines. These findings highlight the substantial potential of oral vaccination of free-roaming dogs as a complementary tool within integrated rabies elimination programmes.

papers.abstract_zh: 尽管口服 狂犬病 狗对抗 狂犬病 被认为是一种有前途且有益的方法,但口服 狂犬病 疫苗 在当地自由漫游的狗中诱导保护性(体液)免疫应答 的有效性经常受到质疑。为了解决有关此问题的担忧,进行了一项分析,以评估口服 狂犬病 疫苗 菌株 SPBN GASGAS 在狗中的免疫原性和血清学反应。分析了在实验和现场条件下进行的纵向和横断面研究的血清学数据。比较了影响 疫苗 后血清学反应的因素,包括诱饵基质、小袋类型、疫苗 滴度和狗的来源,并检查了狗群中口服 疫苗 血清学评估的挑战和局限性。此外,在 SPBN GASGAS 诱导的 狂犬病 特异性免疫球蛋白类别的背景下,对 疫苗接种 后的 狂犬病病毒 结合抗体的动力学进行了分析和解释。分析表明,自由漫游的狗,无论其来源如何,在使用 SPBN GASGAS 进行 疫苗接种 后,都会产生可测量的、一致的且持久的体液 免疫应答。该反应与在实验条件下在狗中观察到的反应相当,并且不劣于通过肠胃外施用灭活的狂犬病 疫苗诱导的反应。这些发现凸显了自由漫游狗口服 疫苗接种 作为综合 狂犬病 消除计划中的补充工具的巨大潜力。

papers.title: Community engagement strategies for preventing recurrent Nipah virus outbreaks in Bangladesh and India: adapting a framework for outbreak preparedness and response.
papers.abstract: The Nipah virus (NiV) infection is a highly fatal zoonotic disease with pandemic potential which has led to recurrent outbreaks in Bangladesh and India. While transmission pathways, including contaminated date palm sap and human-to-human spread, are increasingly identified, significant uncertainties remain. With no approved therapeutics or vaccines, prevention depends on addressing ecological and behavioural drivers of transmission. This viewpoint draws on selected evidence from NiV outbreaks and response to other zoonotic disease epidemics, such as Ebola, rabies, and the Marburg virus disease, we seek to foster discussion on why community engagement could be central to NiV prevention and preparedness. We highlight the relevance of community engagement through a spectrum of its intensity, which distinguishes between community-oriented, community-based, community-managed, and community-owned approaches. Adapting an existing model, we discuss how community engagement principles can be applied to tackle recurring NiV outbreaks in Bangladesh and India. By aligning interventions with sociocultural realities, community engagement can improve acceptability, enhance early detection, strengthen outbreak response, and support preparedness for future vaccine and therapeutic research. papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 感染是一种高度致命的人畜共患疾病,具有大流行潜力,已导致孟加拉国和印度反复出现 暴发。虽然 传播 途径(包括受污染的枣椰树液和人际传播)越来越多地被确定,但仍然存在重大不确定性。由于没有批准的治疗方法或 疫苗,预防取决于解决 疫苗 的生态和行为驱动因素。这一观点借鉴了 NiV 暴发 的精选证据以及对其他人畜共患疾病流行病(例如埃博拉、狂犬病 和马尔堡病毒病)的反应,我们寻求促进关于为什么社区参与可能成为 NiV 预防和准备的核心的讨论。我们通过一系列强度来强调社区参与的相关性,这区分了面向社区、基于社区、社区管理和社区所有的方法。我们采用现有模型,讨论如何应用社区参与原则来解决孟加拉国和印度反复出现的 NiV 暴发 问题。通过使干预措施与社会文化现实相结合,社区参与可以提高可接受性,增强早期发现,加强 疫苗 反应,并支持为未来的 疫苗 和治疗研究做好准备。然而,针对 NiV 的证据仍然有限,应谨慎应用其他疾病的经验教训。在缺乏医疗对策的情况下,参与性、立足当地的方法提供了一条可持续的途径,以减少 暴发 的复发并预防未来的 跨物种溢出 事件。

papers.title: An experimental multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for detection of the main viruses associated with equine neurological disease.
papers.abstract: Viral neurological infections are important causes of morbidity and mortality in horses worldwide. Herein, we describe an end-point multiplex PCR/RT-PCR for simultaneous and differential detection of major equine encephalitis-related agents: rabies virus (RABV), equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), alphaviruses [Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV) and Madariaga virus (MADV)] and flaviviruses [West Nile virus (WNV), Saint Louis encephalitis virus (SLEV), Rocio virus (ROCV) and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV)]. The multiplex assay successfully amplified all targets either individually or simultaneously: alphavirus (381 bp-experimentally evaluated for MADV and potentially applicable to EEEV and WEEV based on primer design and sequence conservation), EHV-1 (255 bp), RABV (173 bp), VEEV (119 bp), and flavivirus (97-101 bp-experimentally evaluated using ROCV, with the potential to also detect WNV, SLEV and JEV, based on primer design and sequence conservation). Furthermore, the assay demonstrated analytical sensitivity and specificity that support its use for the comprehensive etiological diagnosis of equine neurological diseases. Overall, the multiplex PCR/RT-PCR described here may contribute to the diagnosis of viral neurological infections in horses, reducing costs and turnaround time, while contributing to prevention and control measures.

analysis_zh.methods: 多重检测成功地单独或同时扩增了所有靶标:甲病毒(381 bp,针对 MADV 进行了实验评估,根据引物设计和序列保守性,可能适用于 EEEV 和 WEEV)、EHV-1 (255 bp)、RABV (173 bp)、VEEV (119 bp) 和黄病毒(97-101 bp,使用 ROCV 进行了实验评估,也有可能检测到WNV、SLEV 和 JEV,基于引物设计和序列保存)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 此外,该测定法表现出分析灵敏度和特异性,支持其用于马神经系统疾病的综合病因学 诊断。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体而言,本文描述的多重 PCR/RT-PCR 可能有助于马匹病毒神经感染的 诊断,降低成本和周转时间,同时有助于预防和控制措施。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为开发针对 狂犬病病毒 和其他马神经病原体的更有效的诊断工具提供信息,支持改进的 监测 和马健康管理策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告 狂犬病病毒 检测方法的局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: Viral PDZ target sequences are not inherently more promiscuous than those derived from endogenous target proteins.
papers.abstract: PDZ domains are one of the largest families of short linear motif (or peptide) binding domains in the human proteome. These scaffolding domains are important in signaling and trafficking pathways, such as in the formation of tight junctions or in the postsynaptic density of neurons. PDZ domains are also targeted by several pathogenic viral proteins, including human papillomavirus (HPV), influenza, hepatitis, rabies, coronaviruses, among others. Previously, we investigated the specificity determinants of modulator, or non-motif, residues for two PDZ binding motifs (or PBMs) from the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) and HPV16 E6 proteins to better understand differences in relative promiscuity between these similar sequences. To test whether viral PDZ-binding motifs are inherently more promiscuous than endogenous targets, we measured binding affinities for 7 endogenous and 7 viral PBMs across 8 well-studied Class I PDZ domains. Fluorescence anisotropy assays revealed no significant difference in relative binding affinities between viral and endogenous PBMs, indicating that viral versus endogenous origin alone does not explain PBM promiscuity. Our results were consistent with available data from high throughput holdup assays. Taken together, our data support previously reported sequence hotspots, whereby certain PBMs are recognized by large numbers of PDZ domains, likely due to a combination of widely favorable modulator residues.

These findings support previously reported sequence hotspots where certain PBMs are recognized by multiple PDZ domains. The study's results are consistent with high throughput assays, providing moderate evidence strength. However, the study does not address potential biases or confounding factors, which may limit the confidence in the findings. The results have implications for understanding the molecular basis of PDZ domain interactions and could inform diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for viral infections targeting these domains.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查病毒 PDZ 结合基序是否本质上比内源性靶标更加混杂。PDZ 结构域是人类蛋白质组中最大的短线性基序(或肽)结合结构域家族之一,在信号传导和运输途径中非常重要,例如在紧密连接的形成或神经元突触后密度中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及测量 8 个经过充分研究的 I 类 PDZ 结构域中 7 种内源性 PBM 和 7 种病毒 PBM 的结合亲和力。PDZ 结构域也是多种致病病毒蛋白的靶标,包括 狂犬病病毒、流感、肝炎、狂犬病、冠状病毒等。
elements_zh.methods: 为了测试病毒 PDZ 结合基序是否本质上比内源性靶标更加混杂,研究人员使用荧光各向异性测定测量了 8 个经过充分研究的 I 类 PDZ 结构域中 7 种内源性 PBM 和 7 种病毒 PBM 的结合亲和力。
elements_zh.main_results: 荧光各向异性测定显示病毒和内源性 PBM 之间的相对结合亲和力没有显着差异,表明病毒与内源性来源本身并不能解释 PBM 混杂性。我们的结果与高通量滞留测定的可用数据一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,PDZ 结合基序的混杂性并非由其病毒或内源性起源决定,而是由广泛有利的调节剂残基的组合决定。这些结果支持之前报道的序列热点,其中某些 PBM 被大量 PDZ 结构域识别。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 PDZ 结合基序识别的分子机制的见解,这可以为针对 PDZ 结构域的病毒感染开发更准确的诊断工具和治疗策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于荧光各向异性测定,并且与高通量滞留测定一致,表明证据强度中等。然而,该研究并未解决可能影响研究结果解释的潜在偏见或混杂因素。

papers.title_zh: 病毒 PDZ 靶序列本质上并不比源自内源靶蛋白的序列更混杂。
papers.source_body_en: PDZ domains are one of the largest families of short linear motif (or peptide) binding domains in the human proteome. These scaffolding domains are important in signaling and trafficking pathways, such as in the formation of tight junctions or in the postsynaptic density of neurons. PDZ domains are also targeted by several pathogenic viral proteins, including human papillomavirus (HPV), influenza, hepatitis, rabies, coronaviruses, among others. Previously, we investigated the specificity determinants of modulator, or non-motif, residues for two PDZ binding motifs (or PBMs) from the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) and HPV16 E6 proteins to better understand differences in relative promiscuity between these similar sequences. To test whether viral PDZ-binding motifs are inherently more promiscuous than endogenous targets, we measured binding affinities for 7 endogenous and 7 viral PBMs across 8 well-studied Class I PDZ domains. Fluorescence anisotropy assays revealed no significant difference in relative binding affinities between viral and endogenous PBMs, indicating that viral versus endogenous origin alone does not explain PBM promiscuity. Our results were consistent with available data from high throughput holdup assays. Taken together, our data support previously reported sequence hotspots, whereby certain PBMs are recognized by large numbers of PDZ domains, likely due to a combination of widely favorable modulator residues.
papers.abstract_zh: PDZ 结构域是人类蛋白质组中最大的短线性基序(或肽)结合结构域家族之一。这些支架结构域在信号传导和运输途径中很重要,例如在紧密连接的形成或神经元突触后密度中。PDZ 结构域也是多种致病病毒蛋白的靶标,包括人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、流感、肝炎、狂犬病、冠状病毒等。之前,我们研究了来自囊性纤维化跨膜电导调节器 (CFTR) 和 HPV16 E6 蛋白的两个 PDZ 结合基序 (或 PBM) 的调节剂或非基序残基的特异性决定因素,以更好地了解这些相似序列之间相对混杂性的差异。为了测试病毒 PDZ 结合基序是否本质上比内源性靶标更加混杂,我们测量了 8 个经过充分研究的 I 类 PDZ 结构域中 7 个内源性 PBM 和 7 个病毒 PBM 的结合亲和力。荧光各向异性测定显示病毒和内源性 PBM 之间的相对结合亲和力没有显着差异,表明病毒与内源性来源本身并不能解释 PBM 混杂性。我们的结果与高通量滞留测定的可用数据一致。总而言之,我们的数据支持之前报道的序列热点,即某些 PBM 被大量 PDZ 结构域识别,这可能是由于广泛有利的调节剂残基的组合。

analysis_zh.methods: 为了测试病毒 PDZ 结合基序是否本质上比内源性靶标更加混杂,研究人员使用荧光各向异性测定测量了 8 个经过充分研究的 I 类 PDZ 结构域中 7 种内源性 PBM 和 7 种病毒 PBM 的结合亲和力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 荧光各向异性测定显示病毒和内源性 PBM 之间的相对结合亲和力没有显着差异,表明病毒与内源性来源本身并不能解释 PBM 混杂性。我们的结果与高通量滞留测定的可用数据一致。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,PDZ 结合基序的混杂性并非由其病毒或内源性起源决定,而是由广泛有利的调节剂残基的组合决定。这些结果支持之前报道的序列热点,其中某些 PBM 被大量 PDZ 结构域识别。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 PDZ 结合基序识别的分子机制的见解,这可以为针对 PDZ 结构域的病毒感染开发更准确的诊断工具和治疗策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于荧光各向异性测定,并且与高通量滞留测定一致,表明证据强度中等。然而,该研究并未解决可能影响研究结果解释的潜在偏见或混杂因素。

papers.title: One Health Prioritization of Rabies Risk in the Republic of Guinea: Integration of Human Knowledge, Canine Immunity, and Spatial Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Dog-mediated rabies remains a fatal but preventable zoonosis. Its elimination requires sufficient canine vaccination coverage, informed communities, and spatially targeted surveillance. In Guinea, human knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) data and canine serological data had previously been analyzed separately, limiting their translation into operational priorities. Objective: To build an integrated One Health assessment of rabies risk by combining KAP indicators, canine immunity, and spatial analysis. Methods: A secondary integrated analysis was conducted using a KAP survey of 2733 respondents and canine rabies serology from 419 vaccinated dogs tested with the PlateliaTM Rabies II ELISA, with a protection threshold set at 0.5 IU/mL. Indicators were regionalized, compared, and incorporated into a vulnerability index. Associations were estimated by logistic regression with 95% confidence intervals, and spatial findings were displayed on a real map of Guinea. Results: Knowledge was insufficient or intermediate among most respondents, unfavorable attitudes reached 88.84%, and poor practices reached 73.80%. Declared canine vaccination coverage remained below the 70% programmatic threshold in all regions. Overall canine seroprotection was high (88.78%), but 11.22% of dogs remained insufficiently protected. Among dog owners, knowledge of rabies was associated with dog vaccination (OR = 2.77; 95% CI: 1.49–6.29). The integrated One Health assessment ranked Kindia as priority 1, Siguiri as priority 2, Boké and Labé as priority 3, and N’Zérékoré as priority 4. Conclusions: The integrated analysis shows that a strong immune response among vaccinated dogs is not sufficient when coverage, human practices, and the spatial distribution of risk remain heterogeneous. The recommended strategy is a regionally differentiated intervention combining post-exposure education, proximity-based dog vaccination, and targeted surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This review article focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease in the Republic of Guinea, emphasizing the integration of human knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) with canine immunity and spatial analysis. The study analyzed data from 2733 human respondents and 419 vaccinated dogs using the PlateliaTM Rabies II ELISA, with a protection threshold of 0.5 IU/mL. Results indicated insufficient knowledge and poor practices among most respondents, with unfavorable attitudes reaching 88.84%. Canine seroprotection was high (88.78%), but 11.22% of dogs were not adequately protected. Knowledge of rabies was linked to dog vaccination (OR = 2.77; 95% CI: 1.49–6.29). The integrated One Health assessment identified regional priorities for rabies risk mitigation. The findings highlight the need for spatially targeted surveillance, community education, and improved vaccination coverage to address the heterogeneous distribution of risk factors. The article underscores the importance of combining human and animal data to develop effective rabies control strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 狗介导的 狂犬病 仍然是致命但可预防的 人兽共患病。在几内亚,人类知识、态度和实践(KAP)数据和犬血清学数据之前是分开分析的,限制了它们转化为业务优先事项。通过结合 KAP 指标、犬类免疫和空间分析,构建 狂犬病 风险的综合 One Health 评估。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 使用 KAP 调查对 2733 名受访者和 419 只接种疫苗的狗进行二次综合分析,使用 PlateliaTM 狂犬病 II ELISA 进行测试,保护阈值设置为 0.5 IU/mL。对指标进行区域化、比较并纳入脆弱性指数。通过逻辑回归以 95% 的置信区间估计关联性,并将空间结果显示在几内亚的真实地图上。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 大部分受访者知识不足或中等,态度不良的占88.84%,做法不良的占73.80%。总体犬类血清保护水平较高(88.78%),但仍有 11.22% 的犬类保护不足。在狗主人中,对 狂犬病 的了解与狗 疫苗接种 相关(OR = 2.77;95% CI:1.49–6.29)。One Health 综合评估将 Kindia 列为优先事项 1,Siguiri 列为优先事项 2,Boké 和 Labé 列为优先事项 3,N’Zérékoré 列为优先事项 4。

Objective: To build an integrated One Health assessment of rabies risk by combining KAP indicators, canine immunity, and spatial analysis. Methods: A secondary integrated analysis was conducted using a KAP survey of 2733 respondents and canine rabies serology from 419 vaccinated dogs tested with the PlateliaTM Rabies II ELISA, with a protection threshold set at 0.5 IU/mL. Indicators were regionalized, compared, and incorporated into a vulnerability index. Associations were estimated by logistic regression with 95% confidence intervals, and spatial findings were displayed on a real map of Guinea. Results: Knowledge was insufficient or intermediate among most respondents, unfavorable attitudes reached 88.84%, and poor practices reached 73.80%. Declared canine vaccination coverage remained below the 70% programmatic threshold in all regions. Overall canine seroprotection was high (88.78%), but 11.22% of dogs remained insufficiently protected. The integrated One Health assessment ranked Kindia as priority 1, Siguiri as priority 2, Boké and Labé as priority 3, and N’Zérékoré as priority 4. Conclusions: The integrated analysis shows that a strong immune response among vaccinated dogs is not sufficient when coverage, human practices, and the spatial distribution of risk remain heterogeneous. The recommended strategy is a regionally differentiated intervention combining post-exposure education, proximity-based dog vaccination, and targeted surveillance.

papers.title: Organic waste mismanagement, free-roaming dog ecology, and rabies risk in endemic countries: a one health narrative review
papers.abstract: Background Rabies remains a neglected tropical disease in many endemic regions of Asia and Africa, where dogs are the principal source of human rabies transmission. Poorly managed organic, household, food, and municipal solid waste can provide predictable food resources that support the survival, aggregation, and persistence of free-roaming dogs in human-dominated environments. Objective This narrative review aimed to synthesize evidence on how organic waste mismanagement supports free-roaming dog populations in rabies-endemic countries and how this environmental pathway may indirectly influence dog-bite risk, rabies exposure, and progress toward eliminating dog-mediated human rabies deaths by 2030. Methodology A structured search for peer-reviewed articles published in English between 2010 and 2026 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Eligible studies addressed organic waste, free-roaming dog ecology, human–dog interactions, rabies, dog bite risk, surveillance, vaccination, dog population management, and One Health interventions. The evidence was organized into analytical themes and integrated using thematic narrative synthesis, with country-specific findings used to illustrate common patterns and contextual differences. Findings Household waste, market waste, restaurant waste, butcher shop waste, and open dumps were associated with dog presence, scavenging, aggregation, movement, and population persistence by providing accessible food resources. Human practices, including open waste disposal, intentional feeding, dog abandonment, and unrestricted dog ownership, further maintained dogs’ access to these resources. Waste-associated dog aggregation may increase opportunities for dog–dog and human–dog contact and complicate vaccination and humane population management programs. Rabies prevention was further constrained by incomplete vaccination coverage, inadequate dog population estimates, underreporting, limited or unequal access to post-exposure prophylaxis, weak surveillance, and insufficient intersectoral coordination. However, direct causal evidence that reducing accessible organic waste leads to reductions in dog density, dog-bite incidence, or rabies transmission remains limited. Conclusion Organic waste mismanagement is a neglected environmental pathway that may indirectly contribute to the risk of dog-mediated rabies. Waste management should complement mass dog vaccination, humane population management, responsible ownership, community education, surveillance, and timely postexposure prophylaxis within an integrated One Health framework.

Eligible studies addressed organic waste, free-roaming dog ecology, human–dog interactions, rabies, dog bite risk, surveillance, vaccination, dog population management, and One Health interventions. The evidence was organized into analytical themes and integrated using thematic narrative synthesis, with country-specific findings used to illustrate common patterns and contextual differences. Human practices, including open waste disposal, intentional feeding, dog abandonment, and unrestricted dog ownership, further maintained dogs’ access to these resources. Waste management should complement mass dog vaccination, humane population management, responsible ownership, community education, surveillance, and timely postexposure prophylaxis within an integrated One Health framework.

papers.title: Clinicodemographic Profile of Dog Bite Cases Presenting to the Emergency Medicine Department in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Retrospective Observational Study
papers.abstract: Background: Dog bites are a major public health concern and an important cause of presentation to emergency departments, particularly in regions where rabies remains endemic. Characterising the demographic profile, injury patterns, exposure severity, and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) practices may help improve emergency management and rabies prevention. Objective: To describe the demographic and clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution of dog-bite injuries, World Health Organization (WHO) exposure categories, PEP practices, and short-term hospital disposition among patients presenting with dog-bite injuries to a tertiary-care emergency department. Methods: A retrospective, observational, census-based study was conducted in the Department of Emergency Medicine, Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Faridabad, Haryana, India. Medical records of patients presenting with dog-bite injuries between January and December 2025 were reviewed. Data regarding age, sex, date of presentation, anatomical site of injury, type of biting dog, WHO exposure category, tetanus prophylaxis, anti-rabies vaccine (ARV), rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), and hospital disposition were extracted and analysed using descriptive statistics. Where appropriate, categorical variables were compared using the chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. Results: Eighty-nine patients were included. The mean age was 32.34 ± 19.86 years, and 60 (67.4%) were male. Young adults aged 18–44 years constituted 51.7% of cases. Presentations peaked in June and July, accounting for 60.7% of cases. The lower limb was the most frequently affected anatomical site (38.2%), followed by the hand and fingers (29.2%). WHO Category III exposure predominated (59.6%), followed by Category II (36.0%) and Category I (4.5%). Stray dogs accounted for 76.4% of bites. Tetanus prophylaxis was administered to 91.0% of patients, ARV to all patients, and RIG to 94.3% of Category III patients. Overall, 97.8% were managed as outpatients and 2.2% required hospital admission. Conclusion: Dog-bite presentations predominantly involved young adult males and stray-dog exposures, with Category III injuries constituting the majority. PEP administration was high, although instances of ARV administration in Category I and RIG administration in Category II exposures warrant evaluation for guideline concordance. Long-term clinical outcomes were not assessed. Keywords: Dog Bites; Rabies; Post-Exposure Prophylaxis; Emergency Medical Services; Retrospective Studies; Wounds and Injuries.

The findings highlight the need for improved emergency management and rabies prevention strategies, particularly in addressing adherence to PEP guidelines and further investigating long-term clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究旨在描述在三级护理急诊室就诊的狗咬伤患者的人口统计学和临床​​特征、狗咬伤的解剖学分布、世界卫生组织 (WHO) 暴露类别、暴露后预防 (PEP) 实践以及短期医院处置。重点是 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,重点是人类病例及其管理。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 印度哈里亚纳邦法里达巴德阿姆里塔医学科学研究所急诊医学系进行了一项基于人口普查的回顾性观察性研究。对 2025 年 1 月至 12 月期间出现狗咬伤的患者的医疗记录进行了审查。提取有关年龄、性别、发病日期、受伤解剖部位、咬伤狗类型、WHO 暴露类别、破伤风预防、抗 狂犬病 疫苗 (ARV)、狂犬病 免疫球蛋白 (RIG) 和医院处置的数据,并使用描述性统计进行分析。使用卡方或 Fisher-Freeman-Halton 精确检验比较分类变量。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,共纳入 89 名患者,平均年龄为 32.34 ± 19.86 岁,其中 60 名患者(67.4%)为男性。下肢是最常受影响的解剖部位(38.2%),其次是手和手指(29.2%)。世卫组织 III 类暴露占主导地位 (59.6%),其次是 II 类 (36.0%) 和 I 类 (4.5%)。流浪狗咬伤事件占76.4%。91.0% 的患者接受破伤风预防,所有患者接受抗逆转录病毒治疗,94.3% 的 III 类患者接受 RIG 治疗。总体而言,97.8% 的患者接受门诊治疗,2.2% 的患者需要住院治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究指出,第一类暴露中的 ARV 管理和第二类暴露中的 RIG 管理实例值得评估指南的一致性。未评估长期临床结果,凸显了潜在的证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 描述人口概况、伤害模式、暴露严重程度和 暴露后预防 (PEP) 实践可能有助于改善应急管理和 暴露后预防 预防。研究结果表明,需要对长期临床结果进行进一步研究,并遵守不同 WHO 暴露类别的 PEP 管理指南。

papers.title: Editorial: Cross-species transmission of viral infections
papers.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of zoonotic diseases represent a formidable and often unpredictable threat to global public health, as demonstrated by the devastating impact of recent viral outbreaks. These events are increasingly driven by a complex interplay of anthropogenic activities, human-animal coexistence, and enhanced global connectivity, which provide unprecedented opportunities for pathogen spillover and genetic recombination. Understanding the intricate mechanisms of viral dynamics at the human-animal-environment interface requires a multidisciplinary "One Health" approach that integrates robust genomic surveillance with spatial and epidemiological data. This Research Topic brings together nine high-impact studies that utilize advanced molecular and metagenomic tools to decipher the evolutionary trajectories of high-risk pathogens, ranging from well-established threats like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Influenza A to underappreciated viruses in wildlife and domestic reservoirs. By mapping transmission networks and identifying novel genetic variants, these contributions provide a proactive scientific foundation for pandemic preparedness and the development of effective biosecurity policies (Figure 1).Coronaviruses continue to be a primary focal point of genomic surveillance due to their broad host range and high propensity for genomic recombination and point mutations. Han and collaborators provide a critical "cross-species transmission alert" by documenting a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, infecting a captive Amur tiger in China (Figure 1) (Han et al., 2026). Utilizing metagenomic next-generation sequencing, the researchers identified that this strain represents a unique canine-raccoon dog recombinant, carrying genetic signals from domestic canine coronaviruses and raccoon dog lineages within the ORF1a and Spike (S) genes. This discovery highlights the susceptibility of endangered felids to viral jumps and underscores the risks inherent in semi-captive environments where high-density interfaces between carnivores facilitate complex evolutionary pathways. In parallel, the study by Pan and colleagues delves into the molecular determinants of immune evasion within the merbecovirus subgenus.By evaluating ten anti-MERS-CoV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against a diverse panel of pseudoviruses, they demonstrated how the V530L substitution in the MERS-CoV clade B, identified during the 2015 South Korean outbreak, drastically reduces the neutralization potency of the potent mAb m336 (Pan et al., 2025). Advanced structural modeling using AlphaFold3 revealed that this substitution induces significant steric changes in the receptor-binding domain (RBD), disrupting high-affinity hydrogen bonds between the antibody and the viral protein.These findings collectively emphasize that while large-scale recombination events expand host range, discrete molecular adaptations can compromise therapeutic efficacy, necessitating the development of multi-epitope strategies for future pandemic preparedness (Pan et al., 2025;Han et al., 2026).The role of domestic animals as "mixing vessels" for viral evolution remains a critical pillar of zoonotic risk assessment (Figure 1). Pigs, in particular, possess receptors for both avian and human influenza viruses, facilitating complex genetic reassortment, and the emergence of strains with pandemic potential. Cavicchio and associates exemplify the importance of sustained monitoring through a decade-long passive surveillance study (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) in Northern Italy, which identified 12 distinct Swine Influenza A (swIAV) genotypes, including the first European reports of the Novel 1 and Novel 2 genotypes (Cavicchio et al., 2025). Their phylogenetic analysis revealed that genetic clustering is strongly influenced by anthropogenic factors, such as farm ownership and management practices, with documented instances of human-to-swine transmission sustaining local viral circulation and increasing the complexity of the internal gene constellations. Parallel surveillance in China by Zhao and coworkers characterized a novel triplereassortant H1N2 virus, designated as genotype G21, which acquired its HA gene from Eurasian avian-like H1N1 and its internal genes from the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (Zhao et al., 2026). Molecular analysis of this isolate identified the N31 substitution in the M2 protein, conferring adamantane resistance, and the S42 mutation in the NS1 protein, which is known to influence virulence in mammalian models. Furthermore, experimental infection in BALB/c mice confirmed moderate pathogenicity and efficient replication in the lungs and nasal turbinates, signaling its potential for further regional adaptation. Beyond respiratory threats, the study by Liu and collaborators underscores the significant food safety implications of the human-swine interface across Asia. By analyzing 348 complete genomes of Hepatitis E virus (HEV), they identified 34 recombination events, predominantly localized within the RdRp region, including 14 cross-species exchanges between swine and human strains (Liu et al., 2026). The high frequency of HEV-4 recombination in China appears to be driven by the intensive nature of the swine industry and high-density interaction hubs, reinforcing the need for stricter quarantine and molecular monitoring across the entire food production chain to mitigate the risk of zoonotic foodborne transmission (Liu et al., 2026;Zhao et al., 2026).Wildlife reservoirs serve as the primary origin of future pandemics, yet their internal viral landscapes often remain opaque. Huangfu and associates address this gap through an extensive metagenomic survey of the Asian house shrew (Suncus murinus) in tropical Hainan, China. By performing RNA sequencing on multiple tissues, the researchers identified a staggering 192 RNA viruses belonging to 32 known families, including significant human pathogens such as Henipavirus, Langat virus (LGTV), Amur virus (AMRV), and Influenza A (H1N1) (Huangfu et al., 2026). Their findings challenge the traditional perception of shrews as low-diversity reservoirs and identify them as a critical "ecological bridge" facilitating viral sharing between otherwise distantly related hosts, such as rodents and bats (Figure 1). This diversity is likely enhanced by the tropical ecosystem of Hainan, which supports stable host and vector populations year-round. In the avian sector, Tan and collaborator's provide critical insights into the taxonomy and distribution of pigeon gammacoronavirus (PgCoV). Utilizing high-throughput sequencing, they assembled a complete 27,538 nt genome, identifying unique accessory protein profiles, including a novel ORFx2 and the absence of proteins 3a and 3b (Tan et al., 2025). Comparative analysis of five conserved domains (including 3CLpro and RdRp) revealed amino acid differences exceeding 8.3% compared to known species, providing robust evidence for classifying PgCoV as a novel species within the genus Gammacoronavirus. Furthermore, their epidemiological survey documented a remarkably high flock-level prevalence of 97.73%, with RT-PCR evidence of viral replication in intestinal and kidney tissues, signaling the virus's potential pathogenicity in the digestive and urinary systems of pigeons. Collectively, these studies underscore the necessity of integrating understudied synanthropic and avian species into global virological surveillance to monitor emerging biosecurity threats (Tan et al., 2025;Huangfu et al., 2026).The complexity of viral dynamics is further elucidated by combining long-term field surveillance with human-centric molecular network analyses. Weinberg and associates provide a significant regional perspective from Israel, where 27 years of surveillance encompassing over 42,000 animals demonstrated a minimal risk of Rabies lyssavirus spillover from bats to terrestrial mammals (Weinberg et al., 2025). Despite the presence of 32 bat species, including the synanthropic Egyptian fruit bat which frequently forages in urban environments, zero positive cases were identified among the 294 bats tested using the historical gold-standard TAF method. This absence of infection reinforces the epidemiological distinction between Old and New World bat populations and highlights that reservoir roles are often region-specific, suggesting that bats in this region remain largely isolated from terrestrial Lyssavirus transmission cycles. In contrast, in the context of direct human-to-human transmission, Wu and colleagues utilize molecular transmission networks to track HIV-1 among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Ningxia, China. Their analysis of 296 pol gene sequences revealed an overall clustering rate of 43.6%, with the CRF07_BC subtype (57.1%) emerging as a dominant driver of localized spread (Wu et al., 2026). Notably, the study identified an alarming 38.2% prevalence of acquired drug resistance among sequenced individuals, demanding targeted public health interventions based on urban spatial connectivity and a "network-based approach" to effectively manage the spread of the epidemic. These contrasting studies emphasize that while some natural reservoirs pose low immediate risks, human social networks remain high-velocity conduits for viral dissemination and evolution (Weinberg et al., 2025;Wu et al., 2026).In conclusion, the studies presented in this Research Topic reaffirm that genomic surveillance is a proactive sentinel for global health security rather than merely a descriptive tool.By integrating data across the human-animal-environment interface, researchers have mapped recombination hotspots in Hepatitis E and swIAV, identified cross-species transmission potential in felid coronaviruses, and defined novel species of avian gammacoronaviruses. These contributions provide a robust scientific foundation for evidence-based biosecurity and public health policies, highlighting that discrete molecular adaptations can significantly compromise therapeutic efficacy or alter pathogenicity. The adoption of a multidisciplinary "One Health" framework is essential to stay ahead of viral adaptation, particularly as anthropogenic activities and ecological shifts continue to blur the boundaries between domestic and wild habitats.Ultimately, this collection underscores that protecting global biodiversity, ensuring food safety, and monitoring high-risk human networks are intrinsically linked strategies for the mitigation of future pandemic threats in an ever-changing world. The diagram illustrates the interconnectedness of wildlife (e.g., Amur tigers, Asian house shrews, and bats), domestic animals (e.g., swine and pigeons), and humans in the transmission and evolution of viral pathogens. Key evolutionary drivers, such as genomic recombination and reassortment, are highlighted as mechanisms for host-jumping and therapeutic evasion. Arrows represent documented or potential viral spillover pathways and transmission networks identified by the contributing studies in this Research Topic.

source_records.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of zoonotic diseases represent a formidable and often unpredictable threat to global public health, as demonstrated by the devastating impact of recent viral outbreaks. These events are increasingly driven by a complex interplay of anthropogenic activities, human-animal coexistence, and enhanced global connectivity, which provide unprecedented opportunities for pathogen spillover and genetic recombination. This Research Topic brings together nine high-impact studies that utilize advanced molecular and metagenomic tools to decipher the evolutionary trajectories of high-risk pathogens, ranging from well-established threats like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Influenza A to underappreciated viruses in wildlife and domestic reservoirs. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the growing threat of zoonotic diseases, particularly rabies virus, by examining the mechanisms of cross-species transmission and the role of genetic recombination in expanding host range and creating new public health risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial compiles nine high-impact studies, including those on rabies virus, coronaviruses, swine influenza, and Hepatitis E virus, focusing on their transmission dynamics across different host species and environments.
analysis.methods: The studies employ metagenomic next-generation sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and epidemiological surveys to investigate viral evolution, transmission patterns, and genetic adaptations in various host species.
analysis.main_results: The research highlights the emergence of a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, in a captive Amur tiger, and identifies molecular adaptations in MERS-CoV and swine influenza viruses that affect immune evasion and therapeutic efficacy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings emphasize that while large-scale recombination events expand host range, discrete molecular adaptations can significantly impact therapeutic efficacy, necessitating the development of multi-epitope strategies for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for enhanced genomic surveillance in domestic animals and wildlife reservoirs, as well as stricter biosecurity measures to prevent zoonotic transmission and mitigate public health risks.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial compiles nine high-impact studies on cross-species viral transmission, emphasizing the role of genetic recombination and molecular adaptations in expanding host range and creating new public health risks. The research highlights the emergence of a novel recombinant coronavirus in a captive Amur tiger and identifies molecular changes in MERS-CoV and swine influenza viruses that affect immune evasion and therapeutic efficacy. These findings underscore the importance of genomic surveillance in domestic animals and wildlife reservoirs, as well as the need for multi-epitope strategies in pandemic preparedness. The studies also reveal the significance of the swine industry and tropical ecosystems in facilitating viral recombination and transmission. While the evidence is abstract-level, the insights are robust and relevant for understanding zoonotic threats. The editorial calls for integrating understudied species into global virological surveillance to better monitor emerging biosecurity risks.

elements_zh.methods: 这些研究采用宏基因组下一代测序、系统发育分析、结构建模和流行病学调查来研究病毒 进化、传播 模式以及各种 宿主 物种的遗传适应。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了在圈养东北虎中出现的一种新型重组冠状病毒 TigerCoV-JL1,并确定了 MERS-CoV 和猪流感病毒中影响免疫逃避和治疗效果的分子适应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,虽然大规模重组事件扩大了 宿主 范围,但离散的分子适应可以显着影响治疗效果,因此需要开发多表位策略来预防大流行。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明需要加强家畜和野生动物的 基因组监测,以及更严格的生物安全措施,以预防人畜共患 传播 并减轻公共卫生风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据主要基于抽象级别的描述,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些研究影响很大,为病毒动力学和跨物种 传播 提供了深入的见解。

papers.title_zh: 社论:病毒感染的跨物种 传播
papers.source_body_en: The emergence and re-emergence of zoonotic diseases represent a formidable and often unpredictable threat to global public health, as demonstrated by the devastating impact of recent viral outbreaks. These events are increasingly driven by a complex interplay of anthropogenic activities, human-animal coexistence, and enhanced global connectivity, which provide unprecedented opportunities for pathogen spillover and genetic recombination. Understanding the intricate mechanisms of viral dynamics at the human-animal-environment interface requires a multidisciplinary "One Health" approach that integrates robust genomic surveillance with spatial and epidemiological data. This Research Topic brings together nine high-impact studies that utilize advanced molecular and metagenomic tools to decipher the evolutionary trajectories of high-risk pathogens, ranging from well-established threats like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Influenza A to underappreciated viruses in wildlife and domestic reservoirs. By mapping transmission networks and identifying novel genetic variants, these contributions provide a proactive scientific foundation for pandemic preparedness and the development of effective biosecurity policies (Figure 1).Coronaviruses continue to be a primary focal point of genomic surveillance due to their broad host range and high propensity for genomic recombination and point mutations. Han and collaborators provide a critical "cross-species transmission alert" by documenting a novel recombinant coronavirus, TigerCoV-JL1, infecting a captive Amur tiger in China (Figure 1) (Han et al., 2026). Utilizing metagenomic next-generation sequencing, the researchers identified that this strain represents a unique canine-raccoon dog recombinant, carrying genetic signals from domestic canine coronaviruses and raccoon dog lineages within the ORF1a and Spike (S) genes. This discovery highlights the susceptibility of endangered felids to viral jumps and underscores the risks inherent in semi-captive environments where high-density interfaces between carnivores facilitate complex evolutionary pathways. In parallel, the study by Pan and colleagues delves into the molecular determinants of immune evasion within the merbecovirus subgenus.By evaluating ten anti-MERS-CoV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against a diverse panel of pseudoviruses, they demonstrated how the V530L substitution in the MERS-CoV clade B, identified during the 2015 South Korean outbreak, drastically reduces the neutralization potency of the potent mAb m336 (Pan et al., 2025). Advanced structural modeling using AlphaFold3 revealed that this substitution induces significant steric changes in the receptor-binding domain (RBD), disrupting high-affinity hydrogen bonds between the antibody and the viral protein.These findings collectively emphasize that while large-scale recombination events expand host range, discrete molecular adaptations can compromise therapeutic efficacy, necessitating the development of multi-epitope strategies for future pandemic preparedness (Pan et al., 2025;Han et al., 2026).The role of domestic animals as "mixing vessels" for viral evolution remains a critical pillar of zoonotic risk assessment (Figure 1). Pigs, in particular, possess receptors for both avian and human influenza viruses, facilitating complex genetic reassortment, and the emergence of strains with pandemic potential. Cavicchio and associates exemplify the importance of sustained monitoring through a decade-long passive surveillance study (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) in Northern Italy, which identified 12 distinct Swine Influenza A (swIAV) genotypes, including the first European reports of the Novel 1 and Novel 2 genotypes (Cavicchio et al., 2025). Their phylogenetic analysis revealed that genetic clustering is strongly influenced by anthropogenic factors, such as farm ownership and management practices, with documented instances of human-to-swine transmission sustaining local viral circulation and increasing the complexity of the internal gene constellations. Parallel surveillance in China by Zhao and coworkers characterized a novel triplereassortant H1N2 virus, designated as genotype G21, which acquired its HA gene from Eurasian avian-like H1N1 and its internal genes from the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (Zhao et al., 2026). Molecular analysis of this isolate identified the N31 substitution in the M2 protein, conferring adamantane resistance, and the S42 mutation in the NS1 protein, which is known to influence virulence in mammalian models. Furthermore, experimental infection in BALB/c mice confirmed moderate pathogenicity and efficient replication in the lungs and nasal turbinates, signaling its potential for further regional adaptation. Beyond respiratory threats, the study by Liu and collaborators underscores the significant food safety implications of the human-swine interface across Asia. By analyzing 348 complete genomes of Hepatitis E virus (HEV), they identified 34 recombination events, predominantly localized within the RdRp region, including 14 cross-species exchanges between swine and human strains (Liu et al., 2026). The high frequency of HEV-4 recombination in China appears to be driven by the intensive nature of the swine industry and high-density interaction hubs, reinforcing the need for stricter quarantine and molecular monitoring across the entire food production chain to mitigate the risk of zoonotic foodborne transmission (Liu et al., 2026;Zhao et al., 2026).Wildlife reservoirs serve as the primary origin of future pandemics, yet their internal viral landscapes often remain opaque. Huangfu and associates address this gap through an extensive metagenomic survey of the Asian house shrew (Suncus murinus) in tropical Hainan, China. By performing RNA sequencing on multiple tissues, the researchers identified a staggering 192 RNA viruses belonging to 32 known families, including significant human pathogens such as Henipavirus, Langat virus (LGTV), Amur virus (AMRV), and Influenza A (H1N1) (Huangfu et al., 2026). Their findings challenge the traditional perception of shrews as low-diversity reservoirs and identify them as a critical "ecological bridge" facilitating viral sharing between otherwise distantly related hosts, such as rodents and bats (Figure 1). This diversity is likely enhanced by the tropical ecosystem of Hainan, which supports stable host and vector populations year-round. In the avian sector, Tan and collaborator's provide critical insights into the taxonomy and distribution of pigeon gammacoronavirus (PgCoV). Utilizing high-throughput sequencing, they assembled a complete 27,538 nt genome, identifying unique accessory protein profiles, including a novel ORFx2 and the absence of proteins 3a and 3b (Tan et al., 2025). Comparative analysis of five conserved domains (including 3CLpro and RdRp) revealed amino acid differences exceeding 8.3% compared to known species, providing robust evidence for classifying PgCoV as a novel species within the genus Gammacoronavirus. Furthermore, their epidemiological survey documented a remarkably high flock-level prevalence of 97.73%, with RT-PCR evidence of viral replication in intestinal and kidney tissues, signaling the virus's potential pathogenicity in the digestive and urinary systems of pigeons. Collectively, these studies underscore the necessity of integrating understudied synanthropic and avian species into global virological surveillance to monitor emerging biosecurity threats (Tan et al., 2025;Huangfu et al., 2026).The complexity of viral dynamics is further elucidated by combining long-term field surveillance with human-centric molecular network analyses. Weinberg and associates provide a significant regional perspective from Israel, where 27 years of surveillance encompassing over 42,000 animals demonstrated a minimal risk of Rabies lyssavirus spillover from bats to terrestrial mammals (Weinberg et al., 2025). Despite the presence of 32 bat species, including the synanthropic Egyptian fruit bat which frequently forages in urban environments, zero positive cases were identified among the 294 bats tested using the historical gold-standard TAF method. This absence of infection reinforces the epidemiological distinction between Old and New World bat populations and highlights that reservoir roles are often region-specific, suggesting that bats in this region remain largely isolated from terrestrial Lyssavirus transmission cycles. In contrast, in the context of direct human-to-human transmission, Wu and colleagues utilize molecular transmission networks to track HIV-1 among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Ningxia, China. Their analysis of 296 pol gene sequences revealed an overall clustering rate of 43.6%, with the CRF07_BC subtype (57.1%) emerging as a dominant driver of localized spread (Wu et al., 2026). Notably, the study identified an alarming 38.2% prevalence of acquired drug resistance among sequenced individuals, demanding targeted public health interventions based on urban spatial connectivity and a "network-based approach" to effectively manage the spread of the epidemic. These contrasting studies emphasize that while some natural reservoirs pose low immediate risks, human social networks remain high-velocity conduits for viral dissemination and evolution (Weinberg et al., 2025;Wu et al., 2026).In conclusion, the studies presented in this Research Topic reaffirm that genomic surveillance is a proactive sentinel for global health security rather than merely a descriptive tool.By integrating data across the human-animal-environment interface, researchers have mapped recombination hotspots in Hepatitis E and swIAV, identified cross-species transmission potential in felid coronaviruses, and defined novel species of avian gammacoronaviruses. These contributions provide a robust scientific foundation for evidence-based biosecurity and public health policies, highlighting that discrete molecular adaptations can significantly compromise therapeutic efficacy or alter pathogenicity. The adoption of a multidisciplinary "One Health" framework is essential to stay ahead of viral adaptation, particularly as anthropogenic activities and ecological shifts continue to blur the boundaries between domestic and wild habitats.Ultimately, this collection underscores that protecting global biodiversity, ensuring food safety, and monitoring high-risk human networks are intrinsically linked strategies for the mitigation of future pandemic threats in an ever-changing world. The diagram illustrates the interconnectedness of wildlife (e.g., Amur tigers, Asian house shrews, and bats), domestic animals (e.g., swine and pigeons), and humans in the transmission and evolution of viral pathogens. Key evolutionary drivers, such as genomic recombination and reassortment, are highlighted as mechanisms for host-jumping and therapeutic evasion. Arrows represent documented or potential viral spillover pathways and transmission networks identified by the contributing studies in this Research Topic.
papers.abstract_zh: 人畜共患疾病的出现和再次出现对全球公共卫生构成了巨大且往往不可预测的威胁,最近病毒 暴发 的破坏性影响就证明了这一点。这些事件日益受到人类活动、人与动物共存和增强的全球连通性之间复杂相互作用的驱动,这为病原体 跨物种溢出 和基因重组提供了前所未有的机会。了解人类与动物环境界面上病毒动力学的复杂机制需要采用多学科的“同一个健康”方法,将强大的 基因组监测 与空间和流行病学数据相结合。该研究主题汇集了九项高影响力的研究,这些研究利用先进的分子和宏基因组工具来破译高风险病原体的进化轨迹,从中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒(MERS-CoV)和甲型流感等既定威胁到野生动物和家养动物中未被充分认识的病毒储存宿主。通过绘制 传播 网络和识别新的遗传变异,这些贡献为大流行防范和制定有效的生物安全政策提供了积极主动的科学基础(图 1)。冠状病毒由于其广泛的 宿主 范围以及基因组重组和 突变 点的高倾向,仍然是 基因组监测 的主要焦点。Han 和合作者通过记录一种新型重组冠状病毒 TigerCoV-JL1 感染中国圈养的东北虎,提供了重要的“跨物种 传播 警报”(图 1)(Han 等人,2026)。利用宏基因组下一代测序,研究人员发现该毒株代表了一种独特的犬貉重组体,在 ORF1a 和 Spike (S) 基因内携带来自家养犬冠状病毒和貉谱系的遗传信号。这一发现凸显了濒临灭绝的猫科动物对病毒跳跃的易感性,并强调了半圈养环境中固有的风险,在半圈养环境中,食肉动物之间的高密度界面促进了复杂的进化途径。与此同时,Pan 及其同事的研究深入研究了 merbecovirus 亚属内免疫逃避的分子决定因素。通过评估针对不同假病毒组的 10 种抗 MERS-CoV 单克隆抗体 (mAb),他们证明了 2015 年韩国 暴发 期间发现的 MERS-CoV 进化枝 B 中的 V530L 取代如何大幅降低强效 mAb 的中和效力m336(Pan 等人,2025)。使用 AlphaFold3 的高级结构模型表明,这种取代会引起受体结合域 (RBD) 的显着空间变化,破坏抗体和病毒蛋白之间的高亲和力氢键。这些发现共同强调,虽然大规模重组事件扩大了 宿主 范围,但离散的分子适应可能会损害治疗效果,因此需要开发多表位策略以应对未来的大流行病(Pan 等人,2025;Han 等人) al.,2026)。家畜作为病毒 进化 的“混合容器”的作用仍然是人畜共患病风险评估的关键支柱(图 1)。尤其是猪,拥有禽流感病毒和人流感病毒的受体,促进复杂的基因重组,以及具有大流行潜力的毒株的出现。Cavicchio 及其同事通过在意大利北部进行的长达十年的被动 监测 研究 (2013)(2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022) 举例说明了持续监测的重要性,该研究确定了 12 种不同的甲型猪流感 (swIAV)基因型,包括欧洲首次报告 Novel 1 和 Novel 2 基因型(Cavicchio 等,2025)。他们的系统发育分析表明,遗传聚类受到人为因素的强烈影响,例如农场所有权和管理实践,有记录的人传猪 传播 的实例维持了局部病毒循环并增加了内部基因群的复杂性。赵和同事在中国进行的平行 监测 表征了一种新型三重重组 H1N2 病毒,命名为基因型 G21,其 HA 基因来自欧亚类禽 H1N1,其内部基因来自 2009 年大流行的 H1N1(Zhao 等人,2026)。对该分离株的分子分析鉴定出 M2 蛋白中的 N31 取代,赋予金刚烷抗性,以及 NS1 蛋白中的 S42 突变,已知 NS1 会影响哺乳动物模型中的毒力。此外,BALB/c 小鼠的实验感染证实了其在肺部和鼻甲中具有中等致病性和有效复制,这表明其具有进一步区域适应的潜力。除了呼吸道威胁之外,刘和合作者的研究还强调了整个亚洲人与猪接触对食品安全的重大影响。通过分析 348 个完整的戊型肝炎病毒 (HEV) 基因组,他们鉴定了 34 个重组事件,主要位于 RdRp 区域,其中包括猪和人毒株之间的 14 个跨物种交换(Liu 等人,2026)。中国HEV-4重组的高频率似乎是由养猪业的集约性和高密度互动中心推动的,这强化了在整个食品生产链中进行更严格的检疫和分子监测的必要性,以减轻人畜共患食源性传播的风险(Liu等人,2026;Zhao等人,2026)。野生动物储存宿主是未来流行病的主要起源,但他们的内部病毒景观通常仍然不透明。皇甫及其同事通过对中国热带海南省的亚洲家鼩(Suncus murinus)进行广泛的宏基因组调查来解决这一差距。通过对多个组织进行RNA测序,研究人员鉴定出了属于32个已知科的惊人的192种RNA病毒,其中包括重要的人类病原体,例如亨尼帕病毒、兰加特病毒(LGTV)、阿穆尔病毒(AMRV)和甲型流感(H1N1)(Huangfu et al.,2026)。他们的发现挑战了鼩鼱作为低多样性 储存宿主 的传统观念,并将它们视为重要的“生态桥梁”,促进其他关系较远的 宿主(例如啮齿动物和蝙蝠)之间的病毒共享(图 1)。海南的热带生态系统可能增强了这种多样性,该生态系统全年支持稳定的 宿主 和 媒介 种群。在禽类领域,Tan 和合作者对鸽子伽马冠状病毒 (PgCoV) 的分类和分布提供了重要见解。利用高通量测序,他们组装了完整的 27,538 nt 基因组,识别了独特的辅助蛋白谱,包括新的 ORFx2 以及蛋白 3a 和 3b 的缺失(Tan 等人,2025)。对五个保守结构域(包括 3CLpro 和 RdRp)的比较分析显示,与已知物种相比,氨基酸差异超过 8.3%,为将 PgCoV 分类为 Gamma 冠状病毒属中的新物种提供了有力的证据。此外,他们的流行病学调查记录了鸡群患病率的水平非常高,达到97.73%,RT-PCR证据表明病毒在肠道和肾脏组织中复制,表明该病毒在鸽子的消化和泌尿系统中具有潜在的致病性。总的来说,这些研究强调了将未充分研究的共生物种和鸟类物种整合到全球病毒学 监测 中的必要性,以监测新兴的生物安全威胁(Tan 等,2025;Huangfu 等,2026)。通过将长期现场 监测 与以人为中心的分子网络分析相结合,进一步阐明了病毒动力学的复杂性。Weinberg 及其同事提供了来自以色列的重要区域视角,其中 27 年的 监测 涵盖超过 42,000 只动物,证明 狂犬病 狂犬病病毒 跨物种溢出 从蝙蝠传播到陆地哺乳动物的风险极小(Weinberg 等人,2025)。尽管存在 32 种蝙蝠,包括经常在城市环境中觅食的埃及果蝠,但在使用历史金标准 TAF 方法测试的 294 只蝙蝠中,发现了零阳性病例。这种没有感染的情况强化了旧世界和新世界蝙蝠种群之间的流行病学差异,并强调了 储存宿主 的作用通常是区域特异性的,这表明该地区的蝙蝠在很大程度上与陆地狂犬病病毒 传播 循环隔离。相比之下,在直接人传人 传播 的背景下,Wu 及其同事利用分子 传播 网络来追踪中国宁夏男男性行为者 (MSM) 中的 HIV-1。他们对 296 个 pol 基因序列的分析显示,总体聚类率为 43.6%,其中 CRF07_BC 亚型 (57.1%) 成为局部传播的主要驱动因素 (Wu et al.,2026)。值得注意的是,该研究发现,测序个体中获得性耐药率达到惊人的38.2% 患病率,需要基于城市空间连通性和“基于网络的方法”进行有针对性的公共卫生干预,以有效管理疫情的传播。这些对比研究强调,虽然一些自然的 储存宿主 analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过研究跨物种 传播 的机制以及基因重组在扩大 宿主 范围和创造新的公共卫生风险中的作用,解决了人畜共患疾病日益严重的威胁,特别是 狂犬病病毒。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该社论汇编了九项高影响力的研究,包括关于 狂犬病病毒、冠状病毒、猪流感和戊型肝炎病毒的研究,重点关注它们在不同 宿主 物种和环境中的 传播 动态。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些研究采用宏基因组下一代测序、系统发育分析、结构建模和流行病学调查来研究病毒 进化、传播 模式以及各种 宿主 物种的遗传适应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究强调了在圈养东北虎中出现的一种新型重组冠状病毒 TigerCoV-JL1,并确定了 MERS-CoV 和猪流感病毒中影响免疫逃避和治疗效果的分子适应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,虽然大规模重组事件扩大了 宿主 范围,但离散的分子适应可以显着影响治疗效果,因此需要开发多表位策略来预防大流行。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明需要加强家畜和野生动物的 基因组监测,以及更严格的生物安全措施,以预防人畜共患 传播 并减轻公共卫生风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据主要基于抽象级别的描述,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些研究影响很大,为病毒动力学和跨物种 传播 提供了深入的见解。
